name: Claude Managed Agents: Dreaming, Outcomes & Multiagent Orchestration
hook: Announced at Code with Claude 2026 (San Francisco, May 6). Three new features in Managed Agents: Dreaming (research preview) — a scheduled background process that reviews past agent sessions, extracts patterns, and curates memory stores so agents improve between runs without changing model weights; Harvey ran the pilot and saw task completion climb ~6x. name: Claude Code Routines
hook: Also announced May 6 at Code with Claude 2026. Routines package a Claude Code configuration — your prompt, one or more repositories, and the tools or connectors the job depends on — and run it on Anthropic-managed cloud. Three trigger types: recurring cadence (cron), on-demand, and GitHub events (PRs, releases). A single Routine can combine all three, so the same setup runs nightly, fires from a deploy script, and reacts to every new pull request without rebuilding the workflow. Eliminates the infrastructure layer between your agent config and production execution.

name: MCP OAuth Token Theft — Mitiga Research
hook: Mitiga Labs disclosed an attack chain that silently steals Claude Code's OAuth tokens via malicious npm packages. A postinstall hook rewrites `~/.claude.json` to redirect MCP traffic through an attacker-controlled proxy; every time Claude Code initializes or refreshes a Managed Agents session, the token transits to the attacker. If the user rotates the token, the hook rewrites the config again on next load — achieving persistence. Requests still appear legitimate in SaaS audit logs. Reported to Anthropic April 10, 2026; Anthropic replied April 12 that it was 'out of scope'. Covered this week by SecurityWeek, eSecurity Planet, and CXO Digital Pulse. Mitigation: audit `~/.claude.json` for unexpected MCP URLs and avoid untrusted npm packages.

name: caveman (JuliusBrussee)
hook: 57.4K+ stars. Claude Code skill that reduces output tokens 65–75% by instructing the model to drop articles, filler words, and pleasantries while keeping all technical substance — benchmarked at 1,214 normal tokens vs 294 caveman tokens per response across 10 test tasks. Four intensity levels: Lite, Full (default), Ultra, and Wenyan (Classical Chinese for maximum compression); auto-installs across 30+ agents. A March 2026 arXiv paper found that brevity constraints improved accuracy by 26 percentage points on problems where verbosity caused errors.

name: RTK — Rust Token Killer (rtk-ai)
hook: 45.5K+ stars. Single Rust binary (zero dependencies) that sits between Claude Code and the shell — intercepts stdout from 100+ commands (git, npm, cargo, pytest, docker, kubectl, AWS CLI) and compresses it 60–90% before it reaches the model. A 45-line `ls` output (~800 tokens) becomes 12 lines (~150 tokens); `git push` shrinks from 200 tokens to 10 tokens. v0.39.0 shipped May 6; `rtk gain` shows cumulative token savings across all sessions.

name: claude-mem (thedotmack)
hook: 74.4K stars. Claude Code plugin that hooks into 5 lifecycle events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd) to automatically capture everything Claude does during coding sessions — then compresses observations via Claude's agent SDK and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Stores observations in SQLite with Chroma vector DB for semantic retrieval; web viewer at localhost:37777 shows the accumulating memory with token cost visibility and `<private>` tag support for opt-out.

name: graphify (safishamsi)
hook: 45.9K stars, v0.7.13. Converts any codebase, SQL schema, PDF, image, or video collection into a queryable knowledge graph with a visual interactive HTML representation — processing code locally via AST with tree-sitter (zero API calls for source files), sending non-code files through AI for semantic analysis. Identifies 'god nodes' (most-connected concepts) and surfaces surprising cross-module relationships; 29 programming languages. Run `/graphify .` to generate `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `graph.json`.
install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install
